fixture: nca_ask replay — Phase A exit gate
purpose: Frozen replay of the 64 nca_ask calls from the SYNIO Phase 0 baseline corpus (main-only cwd), against a frozen SYNIO index, to demonstrate the Phase A exit gate deterministically across builds. Test-side only — not a product command.

queries.filter: tool_name == mcp__nca__nca_ask AND event_type == post_tool_use (all 64 such events in the frozen orientation corpus — no additional window or filtering applied; this is the corpus's own main-only, cwd-filtered baseline set)
queries.reconstruction_method: Orientation events strip content by design (privacy scrub) and only carry a deterministic event_id = sha256(source_project|session_id|line.timestamp|'post_tool_use'|tool_use_id)[:16] (see src/corpus/events.ts:makeEventId). Recomputed this hash for every mcp__nca__nca_ask tool_use block found in the raw session transcripts backed up at ~/nca-corpus-backup/-mnt-c-dev-synio/ (source_project='synio', matching the manifest's --project value), and kept the block whose recomputed event_id matched one of the 64 target event_ids. Result: 64/64 matched bijectively, 0 collisions, 0 missing — no ambiguity, no window had to be chosen by hand.
queries.raw_transcripts_note: Raw session transcripts for this corpus had already rotated out of ~/.claude/projects/-mnt-c-dev-synio/ by the time this fixture was built; recovered from a prior local backup at ~/nca-corpus-backup/-mnt-c-dev-synio/ (148 session files). This backup is external to this repo and not itself part of the fixture — only its extract (queries.jsonl) is frozen here.
queries.caveat_out_of_scope_project_args: 6 of the 64 recorded calls passed an explicit `project` argument pointing outside the SYNIO codebase: 5 at the Obsidian vault mirror '/mnt/c/Users/jesus/Desktop/Papi_Obsidian_Vault/02-Projects/synio' (that index still exists on disk as of fixture creation, but is NOT frozen by this fixture — it is live, mutable, external state), and 1 at '/mnt/c/dev/webs/synio-web' (that index no longer exists on disk as of fixture creation, so it will resolve to a known_env_error 'No NCA index found' today, which it did NOT do at baseline time — it returned real no-match-fallback content back then). Per task instructions these 6 queries were kept unmodified — not filtered — since the fixture must reproduce the original 64 calls verbatim. The harness's throwaway NCA_REGISTRY_PATH only contains a 'synio' entry, so these 6 do not resolve through it; they fall through to nca_ask's own direct-path resolution and, for the 5 that still exist, hit the REAL live vault index directly (including its normal logQuery/updateNodeScores writes — the same trivial, additive side effect any real nca_ask call against that vault already produces day to day). Their classification under replay is therefore NOT guaranteed stable across time or machines; every report generated by this harness flags them individually. This is a known, unresolved discrepancy — see report.md.

index.description: Snapshot of the SYNIO project's *current* NCA index at fixture-creation time (not a historical reconstruction of what the index looked like during the original May-June 2026 baseline sessions — the task asked for the current index).
index.generator_nca_version_note: Not tracked by the DB itself (no generator-version column). Inferred from schema_version=4 (requires a build with migrations/004_doc_code_edges.ts) and the migration_log applied_at timestamp (2026-06-07), which predates both #54 and #55 — those two fixes do not touch migrations/, so they do not affect this index's schema.

storage.rule_applied: size >= 5MB threshold -> stored OUTSIDE the repo
storage.permissions: chmod 444 (read-only) to reduce accidental mutation; the harness never opens this file directly — it copies it into a fresh tmpdir per run before spawning the MCP server, since toolAsk writes query-log/score-boost rows on every call and would otherwise mutate the frozen fixture.

harness.call_path: Spawns `node <dist>/mcp.js` as a child process and drives it over the real stdio JSON-RPC transport (tools/call, name: nca_ask) — the same transport Claude Code itself uses to talk to this MCP server. This is what 'the same path agents see' means here: mcp.ts has no exports (it calls main() unconditionally at module load and binds process.stdin), so there is no in-process function to import without either touching src/ or hijacking the harness's own stdin. AC5 (test/run.js) validates the same server the same way, over the same transport, for the same reason.
harness.isolation: NCA_DB_PATH and NCA_REGISTRY_PATH point the spawned server at a per-run tmpdir copy of the frozen index and a throwaway single-entry registry ({name: 'synio', root: '/mnt/c/dev/synio', dbPath: <tmp copy>}), so queries carrying project_arg=null or project_arg='/mnt/c/dev/synio' both resolve to the frozen copy, and Migue's real, live /mnt/c/dev/synio/.nca/nca.db is never opened or touched by this harness.
harness.determinism_normalization: Two fields in nca_ask's text output are wall-clock-derived and therefore excluded from any stored/compared content, normalized before classification, golden storage, and diffing (this manifest is the only place absolute run times are recorded, matching the corpus extractor's own convention): (1) the `|t:<epoch_ms>` timestamp token embedded by every NCA|q:... header line -> normalized to `|t:<TS>`; (2) the `[WARN] Index is <N> days old` staleness line (src/mcp.ts:staleWarning, computed from Date.now() vs the frozen DB's fixed parsed_at) -> normalized to `[WARN] Index is <DAYS> days old`, since <N> grows every day this fixture exists and would otherwise break byte-exact comparison indefinitely.

classifier.out_of_scope: project_arg is set and differs from index.root — not executed against nca_ask at all (see queries.caveat_out_of_scope_project_args); reported separately, excluded from every gate denominator.
classifier.direct_hit: JSON-RPC success AND output does NOT match the no-match regex (see no_match_regex below) — real symbol/path data returned for the query.
classifier.no_match_regex: /no matches for '|^\(no results\)$/m — recognizes the current "no matches for '<query>'" phrasing AND the legacy "(no results)" line (an older nca_ask build seen in historical June 2026 tool_results, predating even the current wording). Fixed 2026-09-15: the legacy form was previously unrecognized, silently miscounting 4 historical no-match responses as direct_hit — see historical_baseline.legacy_no_results_fix below.
classifier.clean_no_match: JSON-RPC success AND output matches the no-match regex AND output contains NO [F] section AND output contains no flow-shaped content (no `#name[steps]` pattern).
classifier.noisy_fallback: JSON-RPC success AND output matches the no-match regex AND output DOES contain a [F] section or flow-shaped content — a miss dressed up as an answer (the #54 bug).
classifier.known_env_error: JSON-RPC error whose message matches /NCA schema version mismatch/ (SchemaVersionSkewError, #55) OR the pre-#55 raw form /schema_version \(\d+\) is newer than this build supports/ OR /No NCA index found/ — classified, not counted as a product defect.
classifier.product_error: Any other JSON-RPC error, or a missing/malformed response.

gate.scope: Computed over the 58 in-scope queries only (64 minus the 6 out_of_scope). out_of_scope queries are reported (class + reason) but never enter a gate denominator.
gate.direct_hit_regression (criterion 3, gate: Decided by Replay A (test/replay/replay-a.js), not by this (Replay B) script: direct_hit(build under test) must be a superset of direct_hit(95d52b4 reference build), both replayed against the SAME frozen June-2026 index (baseline-manifest.json), AND 0 content diffs between the two builds' direct_hit output for queries both find. run.js's own replay against the CURRENT index never decides this criterion — it only reads test/replay/replay-a-report.json, which must already exist (run replay-a.js first). See baseline_scoped_direct_hits below for the informational (non-gating) count this replaces as the hardcoded reference number.
gate.clean_no_match: every non-hit, non-error query must land in clean_no_match, not noisy_fallback

historical_baseline.purpose: The original gate used a hardcoded '>= 12', which mixed two populations: the 12 historical direct_hit calls could in principle have included some of the 6 out_of_scope queries, making the 12-vs-58 comparison apples-to-oranges. This computes the correct reference number instead of assuming it.
historical_baseline.method: test/replay/historical.js locates, for each of the 64 frozen event_ids, the tool_use block that produced it in the raw May/June 2026 baseline transcripts (same bijective event_id-hash matching used to build queries.jsonl — see queries.reconstruction_method) and its paired tool_result, adapts that {content, is_error} block losslessly into the {result:{content}}|{error:{message}} shape test/replay/run.js:classify() expects, and classifies it with that exact function (imported, not reimplemented or modified — run.js now exports it behind a require.main guard so `node test/replay/run.js` behavior is unchanged). Writes test/fixtures/replay/historical-classes.json (64 entries: event_id, session_id, query, project_arg, in_scope, cls, detail).
historical_baseline.note_on_distribution: Originally computed as 12/43/4/5 before the legacy_no_results_fix below (see there for the correction); still matches Phase 0's original 12/48/4 once accounted for at that earlier stage (the classifier's finer clean_no_match/noisy_fallback split of the 48 no-match calls, and the classifier's known_env_error regex correctly recognizing the pre-#55 raw message form ('schema_version (4) is newer than this build supports (3)') for all 4 historical hard errors, not just the post-#55 SchemaVersionSkewError message). Numbers here are POST-fix (8/47/4/5).
historical_baseline.legacy_no_results_fix: Fixed 2026-09-15 (commit: see git log for 'fix: recognize legacy no-results replay output'). classify()'s no-match regex only recognized the current "no matches for '<query>'" phrasing, missing an older "(no results)" line format present in 4 of the 12 originally-computed historical direct_hit tool_results (all four May/June sessions predating even that phrasing). Fixed to /no matches for '|^\(no results\)$/m. All 4 flip direct_hit -> noisy_fallback (their June-era output DID include a [F] flow dump, matching the pre-#54 bug shape) — confirmed as the ONLY 4 entries that change across all 64 (diffed old vs regenerated historical-classes.json). baseline_scoped_direct_hits corrected 12 -> 8, which now matches Replay A's reference_direct_hit_count (8) exactly — a strong independent consistency check, since Replay A never depended on historical-classes.json's classification (it replays the raw queries fresh against the reconstructed June index with the corrected classify()).
historical_baseline.note_on_this_number: All 8 historical direct_hit calls (post-fix) happen to be in-scope (0 among the 6 out_of_scope). This number is INFORMATIONAL only (see report-drift.md) — the gate's criterion 3 is decided by Replay A's own reference_direct_hit_count/test_direct_hit_count (replay-a-report.json), not by comparing against this number.
historical_baseline.traceability_anomalies_resolved_by_repla: The 2 anomalies flagged before the legacy_no_results_fix are now both fully resolved, one by Replay A and one by the fix itself. 'withRLSContext': found as direct_hit by BOTH the reference (95d52b4) and test (main) builds against the reconstructed June index (Replay A) — proving it is pure September-index drift (that specific scan is missing a node the code still declares), not an NCA regression, not investigated further by grep/SQL. 'vapi tools manage-appointment build-prompt token-estimator': was never a real historical hit at all — its June-era tool_result read literally '(no results)', which the pre-fix classifier's regex didn't recognize; after the fix it correctly classifies noisy_fallback historically too, and Replay A's historical_reconstruction_limits accordingly dropped from 4 to 0 (nothing left to fail to reconstruct, since the four 'limits' were the same four false positives this fix corrected).

drift_vs_regression_analysis.status: Superseded as the REGRESSION-decision mechanism by test/replay/replay-a.js (Replay A) — the run.js `--compare-dist` flag this section originally described has been removed from the code. This section (and drift.js, still live) now serves Replay B only: a per-query, informational drift/source-text-existence signal for the CURRENT index, reported in report-drift.md, never gating. Replay A is what actually decides whether a historical hit's loss is a regression, by running two builds against one frozen June index instead of inferring from source-text presence.
drift_vs_regression_analysis.purpose: direct_hit landed at 7, not the original baseline's 12, identically on both the pre-fix (19988d3) and post-fix (main) builds. Two explanations were possible: (a) drift — the queried symbols no longer exist in synio at the frozen commit, ~3.5 months after the baseline; (b) an nca_ask search regression introduced sometime between the June baseline and 19988d3, invisible to a pre-fix-vs-post-fix comparison because both post-date June. This was discriminated empirically per query, not assumed.
drift_vs_regression_analysis.method: implemented in test/replay/drift.js (still live) + run.js's now-removed --compare-dist flag (see status above; superseded by replay-a.js). For every in-scope clean_no_match: (1) extract identifier-shaped candidate tokens from the query text (camelCase/PascalCase, UPPER_SNAKE, snake_case, $-prefixed, or path-like — see drift.js for the exact rules); (2) check each candidate's existence via `git grep -F -w` (symbols) or `git ls-tree` substring (paths) against the synio commit the frozen index was built from (e29cb7a1), scoped to the directories NCA actually indexes per .ncaignore (src/, tests/, prisma/, scripts/); (3) classify symbol_absent (no candidate exists — drift) / source_text_present_but_not_retrieved (at least one does) / undeterminable (no identifier-shaped candidate — pure natural-language query); (4) [retired] for every source_text_present_but_not_retrieved case, replay the identical query against an NCA build from the end of the baseline window (commit 95d52b4, last commit at/before 2026-06-26) over the same frozen SEPTEMBER index — a flip to direct_hit there and not on the build under test was treated as a confirmed regression. This single-candidate-query approach is retired; Replay A's whole-index, two-build comparison against a period-correct June index is more principled and now does this job.
drift_vs_regression_analysis.result: 51 in-scope clean_no_match: 10 symbol_absent (drift), 26 source_text_present_but_not_retrieved, 15 undeterminable. All 26 source_text_present_but_not_retrieved candidates replayed identically against 95d52b4 (every one classified noisy_fallback there too, i.e. still a miss, just wrapped in the pre-#54 bug) — 0 regressions confirmed. This is also predicted by a direct diff: `git diff 95d52b4 117b562 -- src/storage.ts` touches only the #55 schema-skew catch block: storage.ts's search()/searchNodes FTS query is byte-identical across both builds. Not fixed — src/ was not touched.
drift_vs_regression_analysis.caveat: source_text_present_but_not_retrieved proves the token exists as TEXT in the scanned tree at that commit — it does not by itself prove NCA's tree-sitter indexer turned it into a queryable node (a match inside a comment, SQL migration, or a non-top-level local variable would count as 'exists' here without necessarily being an indexed node). The empirical build-diff step sidesteps this ambiguity for the regression question specifically (identical behavior on both builds either way), but a 'present but missed' query should not be read as proof nca_ask's indexer is broken for that symbol without checking the frozen index's own nodes table.

replay_a.purpose: The actual regression gate (criterion 3). See test/fixtures/replay/baseline-manifest.json for the frozen June-2026 index's provenance, and test/replay/replay-a.js for the two-build comparison it drives. Kept as a separate manifest/script pair (not folded into this file) because it uses a DIFFERENT frozen index than everything else described here, and must never be confused with or accidentally mixed into the September index this manifest.json otherwise describes.
